narrative: Constructed 2026-08-29 as the worked example of the NEON language (the wider shelf). A three-chair barbershop open till nine with a line out the door on Saturdays, walk-ins welcome, a roast-you-while-we-fade-you house humour; the owner leads with the craft, talks fast and funny, and wants the site to feel like the sign in the window. Fills library holes: playful first-five-seconds, proud + urgent audience, existing_disposable maturity, moment_of_need + steady_rhythm, and ambient_breathing on a dark ground with a typographic hero. Resulting direction: THE SIGN IS ON — near-black end to end, one colour that glows on the headline word and the live indicator, condensed caps at big scale, a hairline-bound marquee of the shop's promise, chrome hairlines instead of boxes. Teaches: the glowing accent word, the marquee ribbon, live-status as a design element, hairline chrome, and the menu-first page where the services list is the pitch.

evidence: their three verbs: Fade / Line / Finish
walk in, sit down, we'll handle it
regulars who know a skin fade from a taper, and kids' parents who don't
they want to look right for something tonight
you sit in my chair, we talk, we figure it out
they want visitors to feel: hyped, welcome, roasted a little
never like: those brown-leather-and-gold barbershop sites
the logo's a pair of clippers off a template; do whatever
tonight, or every other Friday for the regulars

palette.because: P4: the shop performs at night — a near-black stage; one electric colour glows only on the headline word, the LIVE dot and the one button (P3); the leather-and-gold convention is refused (P10).

typography.pairing_logic: Tall condensed caps at poster scale for the sign; a plain grotesque body that gets out of the way — contrast in size and width, kinship in bluntness (alongside, P5).
typography.because: A sign in a window is condensed caps; nothing else reads as the sign.

layout.because: The menu is the pitch: services, prices and hours packed in hairline-bound blocks off-centre under the sign; a busy shop looks busy on purpose.

motion.signature_move: the sign breathes — the glow on the accent word and the LIVE dot swell and settle on a slow loop
motion.because: P8: one move that says 'we're open right now'; everything else is still.

hero_concept.concept_statement: FRESH / CUTS stacked in condensed caps with the second word glowing; a LIVE dot and 'open till 9' at the top corner; beneath the sign, the marquee ribbon — WALK-INS WELCOME · FADES · BEARDS · KIDS — running once across the page.
hero_concept.because: moment_of_need + playful → the first screen answers 'are you open and can I walk in' before anything else.

whitespace.because: A line out the door is the brand; the page is packed like the shop, separated by hairlines not air.

notes: the house jokes become the marquee copy — the ribbon is where the roasting lives
prices sit on the same line as the service with a dotted leader, like a diner menu
the chairs are three hairline-bound cards with the barber's name in caps and a 'next open' time
photos run full-bleed and dark-graded so the one colour stays the only colour
voice_to_visual.because: A fast funny voice becomes a sign and a menu; humour gets a ribbon, not a paragraph.

rule_break.what: the accent colour is allowed to glow — text-shadow and box-shadow tinted with the accent, the one place the platform's flat-colour rule is broken
rule_break.where: hero headline word and the LIVE indicator
rule_break.because: A sign that doesn't glow isn't a sign; the glow is the thesis and it happens exactly twice.

tension.expression: The sign owns the condensed caps, the glow, the marquee; the chair owns the alongside copy, the barbers' names, the 'we'll figure it out' line and the next-open times.
tension.because: All sign reads as a nightclub; all chair reads as a template — the shop is both.

first_impression.feel_in_3s: They're open, they're good, and they're going to talk to me.
first_impression.remember: The glowing word and the ribbon of jokes under it.
first_impression.because: playful + urgent = open-now and welcome, in the same second.

language.because: A night trade with loud conviction, a moment-of-need audience and a refusal of the leather-and-gold convention — one colour that glows, the rest is night; Mural would paint where this shop wants chrome.

distinctiveness_check.notes: Shares the dark-condensed energy of e3 but with one glowing accent (not vivid blocks), an asymmetric sign (not a grid), a breathing motion (not expressive) and a typographic hero (not environment); shares the dark single-accent ground with e6 but is dense where e6 is balanced and breathes where e6 enters.

banned_defaults_avoided: no centered hero over a photo of clippers
no booking widget above the sign

summary_for_practitioner: Your site is the sign in your window. FRESH / CUTS in tall capitals with the second word glowing, a live dot that says you're open till nine, and a ribbon underneath that runs your promise across the page — WALK-INS WELCOME · FADES · BEARDS · KIDS — with your jokes in it. Everything else is dark: services and prices packed like a menu with dotted leaders, three chairs with your barbers' names and next-open times, photos run dark so the one colour stays the only colour. The glow breathes slowly; nothing else moves.
